title: The Shades of New Orleans tape and her emotion
summary: She recalls singing at the piano with him in the broadcast tape; reliving it made her ill for two weeks.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yes. Oh, there's one thing you told about, as I say, I didn't see that program on television, but I did hear the tape of it. Mm-hmm. And I remember you told him when you were ready to go, you stood, I think you stood up at the...
No, I was going to have... He was up at the header stage. It was later where I was stopping at the piano. And he was singing, I'll be loving you always.
So that wasn't at his home then? Mm-hmm. It was another place. I'm sorry to make you think of those things. I know how you must feel.
I can't even read a song now. I don't ever play.
Yeah. I can't even read a song now. Yeah. I'm sorry to make you think of that. I thought maybe that was...
You know, after the tape was made, I was sick for two weeks. Really? Yeah.
But he recovered then, all right, so he got well.
